tasks.notes: fleet/retire.mjs:132/251-252 — `createTag` computes and returns a boolean (`res.code === 0 || alreadyExists(res)`) that both call sites discard. A POST that fails for a real reason (auth, 5xx, a malformed sha) is therefore indistinguishable from a success at the call site; the run is caught only by the subsequent `ls-remote --tags`, which then reports `kept — <tag> is not on the remote` rather than the API error that actually occurred. The deferred verification is the right safety gate and is documented at lines 31-35, so this is not a correctness hole, but the discarded return is dead: either drop the boolean and make `createTag` void, or use it to enrich the `kept` line (e.g. `kept — POST for <tag> failed: <first line of output>`) so the operator sees the cause without re-running the sweep. No Machine clause pins this either way.; fleet/retire.mjs:192-197 and 120-123 — `patchPull` awaits the `gh api -X PATCH` and never inspects `res.code`, and `ghRead` maps any non-zero `gh` exit to `null`, which `pullsToPatch` turns into `[]`. The consequence is a line that misreports: a run whose PATCHes all failed still prints `… <k> PR(s) patched`, and a run whose `pulls?state=closed&head=…` read failed prints `0 PR(s) patched` — indistinguishable from a run that genuinely had no PR to rewrite. Since the branches have already been DELETEd by that point (lines 268-269), a silently failed PATCH leaves permanently dead `/blob/ultra/plan-run-N/` links in the PR body with no signal in the sweep's record. Suggest counting only PATCHes that exited 0 and naming the failures in the line (and, as with the `kept` path, not treating a failed pulls read as an empty list).; M5 reads "For each candidate it reads `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls?state=closed&head=<owner>:ultra/integration-run-N`", but fleet/retire.mjs:257-266 `continue`s out of the loop for a kept run before reaching `pullsToPatch`, so a candidate whose tags did not verify gets no pulls read. The behaviour is the correct one — rewriting a body to `/blob/ultra/plan/run-N/` while the tag is absent or at another sha would replace a live link with a dead one, and the branches deliberately stay — and it is disclosed in the comment at lines 258-259, so it is a lawful divergence rather than a defect. It is however unpinned: exam leg (e) (fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs:690-698) asserts the two pulls reads only over the healthy seam, and leg (d) (lines 654-674) asserts nothing about pulls for kept run 3, so an implementation that did patch a kept run's body would pass the exam unchanged. Suggest adding to leg (d) `assert.deepEqual(linesOf(exec, (l) => l.includes('/pulls?') && namesRun(l, 3)), [], '(d)/M4+M5 a kept run's PR body is not rewritten — its branch links still resolve')`, which turns the disclosed divergence into a graded one.; Coverage gap, not a defect: M4 names two failure shapes — "a listing that omits a tag or shows it at another sha" — and both exam variants at fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs:654-657 (`omitEvidence`, `movedEvidence`) vary only the evidence tag; the plan-tag half of `tagIsAt`/`tagComplaint` (fleet/retire.mjs:149-157, 255) is never exercised with a missing or moved plan tag. The code path is symmetric, so nothing is likely wrong, but `planOk` could be hard-wired true and the exam would still pass. A third `tagVariant` (`omitPlan`) over the same loop would close it.; `fleet/retire.mjs:251-252` discards `createTag`'s boolean return, so `alreadyExists` (line 117) and the return at line 132 are dead code: M3's clause "a POST answering that the reference already exists is not a failure" is satisfied only because no POST result is ever consulted. Exam leg (c) at `fleet/tests/test_retire.mjs:643-650` (the `EXISTS` postAnswer) therefore still passes with `alreadyExists` deleted — it asserts a tolerance the code does not actually exercise. The observable behavior is right (the `ls-remote --tags` verify at line 254 is the authoritative gate), so this is not a correctness defect; the fix is either to delete the unused tolerance and its return value, or to consume it — e.g. treat a POST that failed for some other reason as a run to keep, with `tagComplaint`'s wording on the `kept` line, which would give leg (c) something falsifiable to grade.; The two branch DELETEs (`fleet/retire.mjs:268-269`), the PR PATCH (`patchPull`, lines 192-197) and its call site (line 272) ignore the exec result, while the line printed at 275-279 — which M7 makes the record — states `2 branches deleted, <k> PR(s) patched` unconditionally. A DELETE or PATCH that answered non-zero is reported as done. The sweep is idempotent so nothing is lost (a re-run re-verifies the existing tags and re-issues the DELETE), but the printed record can overstate what happened. Suggest checking `res.code` on both and either counting only the calls that succeeded or naming the failure on the run's line.; M5 says "For each candidate it reads `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls?state=closed&head=<owner>:ultra/integration-run-N`", but the live path reads it only for a candidate whose tags verified (`fleet/retire.mjs:271`); a kept run `continue`s at line 265 before any pulls read. The divergence is the correct behavior — rewriting a PR body to tag paths for a run whose tags did not verify would replace working branch links with links to refs that are not on the remote — and it is disclosed in the comment at lines 257-259. A literal implementation of M5 would be the defect. The Machine text should read "for each retired candidate" (`--dry-run`, which deletes nothing, correctly still reads pulls for every candidate at line 242). No exam leg grades a kept run's pulls read, so no assertion has to change.; unverified: the Claim's real object — the one-time sweep over the 18+18 branch pairs on `popmechanic/ultrapowers` and 7+7 on `popmechanic/ultrapowers-walk` — cannot be settled by this diff. Every `git`/`gh` call in the exam goes through `makeExec({ passthrough: [] })` or a `PATH` shim (as Amendment 10 requires), so the argv shapes are pinned against the plan's prose, not against GitHub: that `gh api -X POST repos/<t>/git/refs -f ref=… -f sha=…` creates a lightweight tag, that a duplicate answers with `Reference already exists` in its output (`output(res)` at line 117 reads stdout+stderr), and that `head=<owner>:<ref>` still matches a PR whose head branch is deleted are all unexercised against the real API. What would settle it: the operator running `node fleet/retire.mjs --target popmechanic/ultrapowers --dry-run` at the gate and reading the printed lines before the live sweep — the dry run issues only the one `ls-remote` and one pulls read per candidate (M6), so it is safe against the real target.

completenessFindings.detail: Residual branch-only record wording outside the plan's scope: `skills/ultrapowers/SKILL.md:154-158` still tells the reader to read `status.json` off the evidence *branch* with `?ref=ultra/evidence-run-<N>` and says it "stays after the VM is reaped", and `:168-169` still calls the evidence branch "never merged and linked from the PR body" — the exact sentence Task 4 removed from `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`'s banner as false. `skills/ultralearn/SKILL.md:19` likewise describes the harvester as reading off the `ultra/evidence-run-<N>` branch, although `skills/ultralearn/scripts/harvest_fleet_runs.py:97-111,144` already falls back to the tag. This contradicts the two-tags literal now settled in `fleet/CONTRACT.md:51-58`, `fleet/RUNBOOK.md:211-215`, `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:30-45`, `fleet/janitor.mjs` and `fleet/retire.mjs`. It is not a shortfall of any task: no task's Files block names a skill document and the plan's Global Constraints forbid editing `skills/ultrapowers/SKILL.md`, so the gap is deliberate and belongs in a follow-up, not in this merge.

Task 1 (`fleet/retire.mjs`), Machine slot M5: M5 says "For each candidate it reads `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls?state=closed&head=<owner>:ultra/integration-run-N`", but in the non-dry-run path a *kept* candidate returns at `fleet/retire.mjs:259` before `pullsToPatch` is reached, so no pulls read is issued for it (a dry run does read pulls for every candidate). The behaviour is deliberate and documented in the comment at `fleet/retire.mjs:252-253` — a kept run keeps its branches, so its PR's branch links still resolve and rewriting them would break them — and it does not touch the operator's Claim, which says nothing about PR bodies. Worth an issue to reconcile M5's wording with the code; not a reason to hold the run.
